tourism.detail: The official eTA is required for an Australian visitor. Standard fees begin at USD 30, processing is generally three business days and the border officer decides the stay.
tourism.next: Apply through etakenya.go.ke, download the approval PDF and carry the itinerary, accommodation and return travel.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.route: Business-purpose eTA for meetings and exploration
meetings.detail: The eTA process accepts a Kenyan company invitation and its registration certificate. Use this lane for discussion, networking, due diligence and site visits without delivering a profession or service.
meetings.next: Describe the trip accurately as business meetings and move any added consulting, workshop or demonstration to a Special Pass.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: The eTA service can request a conference invitation or participation letter. Delegate or participant entry does not replace a Special Pass for professional delivery.
conference.next: Obtain the organiser letter and state whether the traveller is only attending or is also presenting, facilitating, exhibiting or working.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Special Pass where the talk is temporary professional activity
unpaid-speaking.detail: The Special Pass expressly covers temporarily conducting a profession. Kenya's eFNS service warns that business or employment without the required permit or pass is an offence; absence of a fee does not settle classification.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Kenyan host seek immigration classification and obtain the Special Pass before the talk where required.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.detail: The host-backed Special Pass can cover temporary professional delivery for up to six months and costs a non-East African USD 200 per month after approval. KRA lists non-resident professional, training and appearance or performance fees at 20% final withholding.
paid-speaking.next: Have the host obtain and pay for the pass before work begins and remit withholding within five working days of payment.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Business eTA for rights meetings; Special Pass and local publisher for active launch
book-launch.detail: Rights and publisher meetings can stay in the business-visitor lane. A programmed reading, promotional service, fee, imported stock or local sale should be handled separately through the host, publisher, customs and tax channels.
book-launch.next: Use a Kenyan publisher or bookseller for import, stock and receipts and have it sponsor any Special Pass needed for the author appearance.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: Special Pass for short professional training; employment permit for continuing work
ai-teaching.detail: A short AI workshop, guest lecture or staff training can be temporary professional activity under a Special Pass, with qualifications and any regulator clearance. A continuing job needs the relevant work permit rather than repeated visitor entries.
ai-teaching.next: Have the institution state whether the session is a guest event, contracted training, research or employment and sponsor the matching pass or permit.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.detail: Class N covers a foreign employer, work for a foreign company or self-employed services to clients outside Kenya. It is issued for one or two years and is renewable. The current page requires three months of bank statements or payslips, accommodation, an employer or company letter and a no-objection letter from the Australian mission; it does not publish a fixed income threshold. Fees are USD 200 processing and USD 1,000 issuance per year.
remote-work.next: Build the Class N pack and keep Kenyan employers and clients outside the remote-work lane unless another permit authorises them.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: Class G permit for specific trade, business or consultancy
entrepreneur.detail: Class G requires licences or registrations, proof the activity benefits Kenya, company and tax documents, and at least USD 100,000 capital available for investment. Immigration and business registration remain distinct.
entrepreneur.next: Use the first eTA visit for exploration, then incorporate, secure sector licences, evidence capital and apply for Class G before operating.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Business eTA for negotiations; Special Pass or Class G for active trade
trade.detail: Supplier and distributor meetings can fit the business eTA. Temporary professional trade activity can use the Special Pass; a continuing local trade or consultancy belongs under Class G. Imports, samples and sales also need Kenya Revenue Authority and customs planning.
trade.next: Appoint a Kenyan importer or distributor and classify meetings, demonstration, installation, local sale and continuing operation separately.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Special Pass plus promoter, venue and tax arrangements
artist.detail: A temporary artistic or performance engagement can be professional activity requiring the pass. KRA lists non-resident appearance and performance fees at 20% final withholding; venue, filming, content and merchandise permissions remain separate.
artist.next: Use a Kenyan promoter to sponsor the pass and document venue approval, tax, equipment and merchandise before public announcement.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: eTA for passive visitor activity plus Special Pass, Class N or Class G for active components
mixed-mission.detail: A trip may combine IGF attendance, local meetings, community AI training, remote work, a book event and a performance. Each line has a different trigger, even when one host coordinates the itinerary.
mixed-mission.next: Make one activity ledger by date, county, host, payer, audience and customer location, then attach eTA, Special Pass, Class N or Class G to each line.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

volunteering.detail: Smartraveller: it's illegal to work or volunteer in Kenya without a valid work permit.

filming.route: KFCB filming licence through a registered local agent
filming.detail: No filming without a KFCB licence. Foreign productions must use a KFCB-registered local agent; licences are tied to the project and dates.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Kenyan Shilling (KES). Declare all amounts over US$10,000 when you arrive and depart. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. Large banks and foreign exchange bureaus continue to accept traveller's cheques, but they can be difficult to cash and attract high fees. Hotels don't usually accept them. ATMs in Nairobi and major towns accept international credit cards. Take care when paying with credit cards or using ATMs. Card skimming incidents are increasing. Only use ATMs at large shopping centres or in banks. Check the machine for unusual parts before you use

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A Kenyan organisation supplies the stamped Special Pass application, detailed cover letter, registration certificate and any regulatory clearance for speaking, teaching, consulting, performance or other temporary professional activity.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Apply only through the official eTA service, normally at least three working days ahead. Carry a passport valid six months, itinerary, accommodation and any conference or business invitation and company registration documents.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The eTA must be used for travel within 90 days of issue; the authorised stay is decided at the border. A Special Pass can cover up to six months. Class N is issued for one or two years and is renewable.

visa-preparation.recheck_note: A trade report says a Kenyan court suspended the insurance mandate in late August 2026 while the portal still enforces it; payment-gateway fees may add a few dollars. Recheck before travel.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Kenya has conservative dress and behaviour standards, especially in coastal and rural areas. You should dress modestly; wear loose-fitting clothing that covers your shoulders, knees, midriff, chest and back. Take care not to offend. The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in Kenya. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. Muslims don't eat, drink or smoke between sunrise and sunset during Ramadan. If you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Public displays of affection can lead to harassment, particularly for same-sex couples. Kenya Tourism Board booklet: ask before photographing people. A small payment may be expected. Dress modestly in towns, villages and coastal Muslim areas.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: KCAA publishes a list of Remote Operator Certificate (ROC) holders. Commercial drone work needs a ROC, and the 2020 regulations require the applicant to have its principal place of business in Kenya and a defence ministry security clearance. Drones need registration, authorisation to operate and an import permit.

items.text: KCAA publishes a document listing ROC holders by company.

Under the Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Systems) Regulations 2020, an operator using a UAS for commercial activities, reward or hire must obtain a Remote Operator Certificate. Applications are made at least 90 days before the intended operation. KCAA's fee schedule lists the initial ROC at 80,000 and renewal at 50,000 (currency not stated in the excerpt read).

The 2020 regulations require a ROC applicant to have its principal place of business in Kenya and to hold a defence ministry security clearance. The older 2017 regulations allowed a 30-day temporary permit (renewable once) for a drone not registered in Kenya; whether it still applies was not confirmed. Operating a UAS needs KCAA authorisation, and importing one needs a KCAA permit.
